newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Eurotax to be submitted as amendment - Visco.
newsitem.headline: Italy Eurotax to be submitted as amendment - Visco.

text.p: The Italian government's plan to raise 12.5 trillion lire next year to help Italy meet the terms for Europe's planned single currency will be submitted to parliament as an amendment to the 1997 budget, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said on Monday.
He told the Senate (upper house) budget commission that the plan would be presented "in the form of one or more amendments" to the budget.
The 1997 budget, which aims to cut next year's deficit by an overall 62.5 trillion lire, is making its way through the upper house after passage by the lower Chamber of Deputies.
Any change to the package in the upper house means it must return to the Chamber for a further reading.
The 12.5 trillion lire special revenue measures include a one-off hike in income tax, popularly dubbed the Euro-tax, which the centre-left government has said will be partly reimbursed in 1999.
